chapter: Looking back: rock, blues, childhood and guitar innovators
title: Timeless stylists: Roy, Erroll Garner and Dizzy
summary: Collins says individualists like Garner and Dizzy never changed and are as enjoyable now.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: And as I say, I was just thinking when I saw Roy, well, gee, nothing -- this man is just as great now as he was then. You know. And this is a sign of a great musician, and a stylist and an individualist. Now, there are many that we think of Errol. See, Errol Garner, he had his own individual style. The first time I heard him it was the same way. I heard him in Pittsburgh. He played then the way he plays now, and it's timeless, you know.

Now, in the meantime there came the bebop era when all the piano players were playing the bebop era. But Errol was Errol. Dizzy was Dizzy. You understand what I'm getting at. And I enjoy hearing them just as much now as I did then. You know, I played a concert last night with my little group, and the first part of the program was devoted to young black musicians, and they had the youth band and they graduated to some, you know, a little older, and they'd have another group, and it was nice.
